one_liner: Small BLIS-style C framework for real L3 BLAS with NEON/AVX2 kernels; matches single-threaded OpenBLAS on Apple M4.
what_it_does: MuBLIS is a C17 framework for building a real-valued Level-3 BLAS: a generic frame handles packing, cache tiling and the loop nest, and each hardware target supplies GEMM and fused GEMM-TRSM micro-kernels plus block sizes (about 200 lines). The built library exports the standard CBLAS signatures for sgemm/dgemm, symm, syrk, syr2k, trmm and trsm, plus mublis_* mirrors that return an error code and a general L3 driver (mublis_l3_sdriver/ddriver) whose iteration space the caller can specify. Bundled configs cover Apple Silicon, Linux aarch64, Linux and macOS AVX2, and a portable reference build.
how_it_is_fast: It uses the BLIS/Goto layered loop nest: B is packed into kc x nc panels, A into mc x kc blocks, and a register-blocked micro-kernel computes one mr x nr tile of C (12x8 for f32 and 6x8 for f64 on the Apple 'firestorm' target) with NEON FMA intrinsics, full unrolling and a software prefetch of the next C tile. The out-of-place routines (GEMM, SYMM, SYRK, SYR2K) are thin shims over one L3 driver that skips or restricts blocks according to matrix structure; TRSM uses fused GEMM-TRSM micro-kernels, and TRMM sizes its triangular blocks from the cache block and the matrix size. Pack buffers are recycled from a pool rather than allocated on every call.
when_to_use: You are bringing up a CBLAS Level-3 library on new or unusual hardware and want the packing and tiling framework done, so that you only write micro-kernels and block sizes.
Single-threaded real f32/f64 GEMM, SYMM, SYRK, SYR2K or TRSM on Apple M-series or other NEON CPUs, where its README chart shows it within about 1% of single-threaded OpenBLAS.
Multithreaded applications that call BLAS concurrently from many threads, each on its own small or medium problem: the library is reentrant and pools its pack buffers.
Teaching or studying a compact, readable BLIS-style implementation in plain C with intrinsics rather than assembly.
when_not_to_use: You want more speed than OpenBLAS: the published gains are 0.2-1% (within noise), and TRMM is about 13% slower (95.8 vs 110.3 GFLOP/s on M4).
Large matrices that should use every core: there is no internal multithreading, and all published numbers are single-threaded.
Complex types, Level 1/2 routines, or Fortran BLAS symbols (dgemm_): none are implemented, so it cannot back LAPACK on its own.

Apple Silicon throughput work: its kernels are NEON only; the catalogued Apple siblings (sme-gemm, MTGEMM-A) report Accelerate's SME/AMX path at about 2 TFLOP/s f32, against MuBLIS's 111 GFLOP/s on one core.
Production use that needs maturity: the project started in July 2026, has 2 stars, and its own README calls its correctness tests non-comprehensive.

integration.form: static lib and shared lib (make CONFIG=<config> builds build/<config>/lib/libmublis.a and libmublis.so/.dylib)
integration.min_toolchain: C17 compiler (CSTD=c17) and GNU make; clang gets a --target triple from the config, while GCC is used without one
integration.platforms: Apple Silicon (firestorm NEON target, -mcpu=apple-m1), Linux aarch64 (NEON), Linux and macOS x86-64 with AVX2+FMA, plus a portable reference config
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant: the target context is chosen once under pthread_once, and pack buffers come from a mutex-guarded pool that grows when more threads call at once; each call runs on the calling thread only.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it covers the real single- and double-precision Level-3 CBLAS routines (gemm, symm, syrk, syr2k, trmm, trsm) with the standard signatures, but not complex, Level 1/2 or Fortran-ABI BLAS

gotchas: Every bundled micro-kernel target is compiled with -ffast-math, so IEEE NaN/Inf and signed-zero behaviour inside GEMM is not guaranteed to match OpenBLAS or reference BLAS.

The bundled configs do not detect the CPU at runtime: linux_avx2's dispatch.c always returns the AVX2 context although the reference target is also linked in, so that build will fault on x86 CPUs without AVX2/FMA. The 'fat binary' support means you write your own dispatch function.

test/performance/benchmark_cblas.py times only one library per run (switch with MUBLIS_LIB) on all-ones and identity inputs; there is no committed OpenBLAS harness, and the README's matrix sizes, compiler and OpenBLAS version are not stated.
Cache block sizes are fixed constants per target, not read from the CPU, so a CPU with different cache sizes needs retuning in the target's context.c.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MuBLIS over GEMMFIP (the BLIS fork) or OxiBLAS when you need a small, readable C framework to port Level-3 BLAS to new hardware, or a reentrant single-threaded CBLAS on NEON. For raw speed, OpenBLAS itself, Accelerate, or the SME-based siblings sme-gemm and MTGEMM-A on Apple Silicon are faster or equal.
verified_claims_summary: The README chart for an Apple M4, single thread, f32, shows MuBLIS against an OpenBLAS built for that machine: GEMM 111.0 vs 109.9 GFLOP/s, SYMM 109.7 vs 109.5, SYRK 109.4 vs 108.8, SYR2K 109.4 vs 109.0, TRSM 100.9 vs 100.2, and TRMM 95.8 vs 110.3. That is parity on five routines and a loss on TRMM; matrix sizes, compiler, flags and OpenBLAS version are not given, and the AVX2 results on Xeon Gold 6248R, Ryzen 7 7700X and i5-7500 are described without numbers.
status_note: Active (first commit July 2026, last 2026-09-01) and MIT-licensed, small enough to vendor, but a 2-star single-author project with limited tests.
